beats.say: Albert Einstein proposed that gravity is actually matter bending space and time.
Centuries before his 1915 theory, Indian astronomer Brahmagupta proposed gravity as an attractive force in 628 CE.
In 1551, Domingo de Soto observed that bodies in free fall accelerate at a uniform rate.
Simon Stevin tested this in 1586 by dropping two cannonballs from the Delft tower.
Despite their different weights, he found they hit the ground at exactly the same moment.
This means gravity acts on all objects equally, regardless of how much they weigh.
Einstein's theory later showed that massive objects bend the fabric of reality itself. That was Science Explained, subscribe so you never miss our next episode.
How often do you think about how gravity works?

facts: Albert Einstein proposed the general theory of relativity in 1915.
Brahmagupta proposed the idea of gravity in 628 CE.
Simon Stevin observed that two cannonballs of differing sizes and weights fell at the same rate in the 1586 Delft tower experiment.
Domingo de Soto wrote in 1551 that bodies in free fall uniformly accelerate.
